newsitem.title: CHILE: Kon-Tiki copycat voyage not credible, says expert.
newsitem.headline: Kon-Tiki copycat voyage not credible, says expert.

text.p: The goal of a Spanish adventurer to sail a reed boat across the Pacific in a recreation of an ancient Polynesian voyage is based on dubious historical ideas, said a Chilean expert on Monday.
Anthropologist Claudio Cristino, a Chilean anthropologist, called the project "an academic scandal" based on historical premises that had long been discredited as "complete stupidities."

Spanish adventurer Kitin Munoz built the 100-foot (30-meter) long vessel, meant to be a replica of primitive ships used before the arrival of Europeans on the South Pacific island, on a beach on Easter Island and plans to sail it to New Zealand via Samoa.

With a multinational crew and a message of peace and brotherhood, the project won funding from the government of Chile, the Spanish royal family, the U.N. Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation and various companies.

Spanish Prince Felipe, son of King Juan Carlos who is a patron of the voyage, came to Easter Island for the launching on Sunday of the fragile boat, the Mata Rangi, but bad weather delayed the launch.

One of Chile's leading experts on Polynesian culture, Cristino said the project was a nice idea based on a phony premise that the island received cultural influences from the Western Pacific -- an idea now discredited, he said.

There was no evidence that the original Polynesian inhabitants of Easter Island ever built ships 100 feet (30 meters) long, said Cristino, local representative of the University of Chile's Easter Islands Studies Institute.

The Mata Rangi expedition is aimed at showing that the peoples of Easter Island, a speck of land in the South Pacific now owned by Chile, may have had links with cultures towards Asia, rather than with South America.

Munoz said in Tahiti last week that he considered himself the "spiritual son of Thor Heyerdahl," who sailed from Peru to Easter Island in 1947 in an epic voyage on a balsa raft known as Kon-Tiki. That voyage showed that Easter Island and other coral atolls might have been populated from South America.
